title: Review of c29's kernel-drive seeds 2-3 finding: replicates on fresh seed 4 (L rim/core 1.53, 229 persistent splits, generation 7, max 5.8 BL) and survives a true dt/2 of the world's own step on the same seed (1.55, 207, generation 7, max 4.5 BL)
summary: Re-ran world.py with WORLD_P {drive kernel, mu 1.0, kd 0.08, chi 5} on fresh seed 4 (labkit, 256^2, t=10000) and with the world's own step halved (dt 0.5, 100 steps per frame, same physical time; labkit labels the time 20000 because META dt stays 1.0). Default step: L rim/core 1.53, rim/out 8.95, 760/1112 individuals membrane-like; 640 splits, 229 persistent, generation 7, merge/split 0.24; 122 tracks >= 1 body length, max 5.8. dt/2: L 1.55, 8.76, 770/1104; 567 splits, 207 persistent, generation 7, merge/split 0.30; 114 tracks, max 4.5. (My earlier seed-3 run, 20261026T0505-c33-review-kernel-ring, gave the finding's seed-3 numbers exactly.)

observations.M: rerun FACTS: 122 tracks >= 1 BL, max 5.8; dt/2 max 4.5
observations.D: rerun/lineage.png: 229 persistent splits, generation 7; dt/2 207, generation 7

seeds_run.result: pass at the default step and at a true dt/2

verdicts.limitation: Labkit only; I did not run ringtrack on seed 4, so the same-lineage swim + ring + divide count rests on the finding's seed 2 and my earlier seed 3 (1 lineage). The colonization-then-jam limit holds at both steps. No resolution test.
